rationale: No supported optimization has verifiable prerequisites for this workflow. The closest pattern, P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (dependency_cache), requires repeated dependency fetching with cache inputs that include a lockfile/dependency manifest plus environment. This workflow installs system packages via tools/ci.sh (apt) in each job and references no lockfile or pip manifest (e.g., pyproject.toml/requirements.txt) in its steps, so a dependency cache key cannot be reliably tied to dependency changes; the only existing cache (qemu_mips MIPS toolchain tarball) already covers the one large repeatable download. Other patterns do not apply: there is no matrix (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST), no schedule trigger (P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE/P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE), no Bazel (P-LIT-BAZEL-*), concurrency with cancel-in-progress already implements P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE, and test selection/prioritization would reduce required coverage (contraindicated). A custom timeout is unsupported because jobs complete well within default limits with no runaway-duration evidence. Adding an unverified pip cache to an apt/toolchain-driven C build would not preserve or improve coverage and risks being ineffective.
